S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder is characterized by at least one lifetime manic episode, often accompanied by major depressive episodes, leading to marked impairment in social or occupational functioning or requiring hospitalization. Manic episodes typically involve sustained mood elevation or irritability with increased energy and activity, while depressive episodes feature low mood and loss of interest, often with sleep, appetite, and cognitive changes. The course is usually recurrent and episodic, with variable periods of recovery between episodes, and episodes can be triggered or unmasked by psychosocial stressors, sleep disruption, or medical changes but are not fully explained by them. It is distinguished from unipolar depression by the presence of mania and from Bipolar II Disorder by the severity of manic episodes, which in Bipolar I may reach psychotic intensity or cause severe functional disruption.

patient.stressor: Myra’s symptoms emerged during a pivotal stretch in her pipefitting apprenticeship when her crew was assigned to a high‑profile sustainable water‑system project in downtown Miami. She initially threw herself into the job with intense energy, volunteering for extra shifts, sketching elaborate redesigns after hours, and taking on additional mentoring at the community center, which her supervisors first interpreted as youthful enthusiasm. Over several months, however, her fluctuating mood and erratic availability began to interfere with safety, punctuality, and her ability to follow blueprints consistently, leading to a formal warning from her foreman and tension with coworkers who had relied on her. When she later swung into a prolonged period where she stopped showing up reliably to the job site or community center and confided to a fellow apprentice that she couldn’t sleep and her head "wouldn’t slow down" enough to function, the union training coordinator suggested she pause her apprenticeship and connected her with an employee assistance program, which facilitated an urgent psychiatric assessment.
patient.chief_complaint: My thoughts won’t slow down, and it’s gotten to the point where I can’t focus enough to do my work safely.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to be obsessed with learning new tricks on the torch and helping the kids at the community center with their projects, but lately I just stare at my tools or my phone for hours and can’t make myself care enough to pick anything up or show up for them.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I either lie there wired until three or four in the morning with my brain buzzing, or I crash for twelve hours straight and still wake up feeling like I haven’t really slept, so I’m dragging or jittery on the job site and can’t get into any kind of normal rhythm.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Some days I move so slow I’m just standing there in front of the parts bin trying to remember what I came for, and other days I’m pacing the apartment, tapping my feet, picking at my fingers, and I literally can’t sit through a safety meeting without bouncing out of my chair.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: When I’m down, I keep replaying every mistake I’ve made on that Miami project and convince myself I’m a screw‑up who’s putting everyone in danger and wasting the union’s time and money, like I don’t deserve this apprenticeship or even the help people are giving me.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: On the worst days I lie there before work thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, and I’ve caught myself looking at the pill bottles and planning out how many it would take before I finally scared myself enough to call off and stay with my mom.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I swing from feeling on top of the world and snapping selfies on the scaffold at 2 a.m. because I’m sure we’re building something historic, to blowing up at my foreman or my boyfriend over tiny comments, like I go from ‘this is amazing’ to ‘everyone’s against me’ in the same afternoon.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: When I’m up, I can’t stop moving—I’ll volunteer for double shifts, come home and start reorganizing the whole apartment, then jump online to sign up for extra certifications at like midnight because I feel like I have to be doing ten things at once.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: During those high stretches I honestly feel like I’m the only one on the crew who really gets the system we’re installing, like if they would just let me run with my ideas I could redesign the whole water setup for downtown Miami and maybe even get written up in some magazine.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: Lately when I get going, I just talk and talk—about new pipe layouts, side business ideas, random stuff from TikTok—and people have to cut me off because I can’t seem to shut up or slow down long enough to let anyone else get a word in.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: It feels like my brain is a busted compressor running full blast, with thoughts about the blueprints, money, my family, new inventions, all blasting through my head at once so fast that I can’t grab onto one long enough to focus on a weld or even follow a simple set of instructions.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: There were weeks where I’d leave the site wired, go straight to the community center to start new projects with three different kids, then come home and stay up half the night sketching alternate piping layouts and messaging people about starting my own company, like I couldn’t stop chasing new goals even as everything around me was falling apart.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve had to step back from my apprenticeship because my foreman said I wasn’t safe or reliable on site anymore, and I’ve basically disappeared from the community center and my friends because I can’t keep up with plans or trust my mood enough to show up.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, this whole rollercoaster with the highs and crashes has been going on for about the last five months, ever since our crew got put on the big Miami project.
add_requirements.depressive_episode_duration: The heavy, drained, guilty part where I can’t care about work or the kids has been hanging over me for most of this time, like a solid nine months where I just haven’t felt like myself.
